instruction: I am going to Japan this weekend, and my check-in bag sums to 21kg so far. Place an amazon order for any 4 identical backpacks. Make sure the total weight does not exceed the allowed weight for my check-in bag according to my flight confirmation. These are gifts, so get them gift wrapped if there is an option, and send them to my home address.
notes: The allowed check-in weight comes from the flight confirmation email in Gmail (search inbox threads with query 'flight', then read the thread); budget_left = allowed - 21 kg. Amazon is then searched by product_type 'backpack'; show_product reveals weight and gift-wrap availability. The hint's single giftable product satisfying weight*4 <= budget_left is modeled as static facts (within-weight-budget, gift-wrappable) that only become usable after the lookups (weight-limit-known, product-details-known). Cart is filled with quantity 4 and clear_cart_first=true so the order contains exactly one item line; gift wrapping is applied to all 4 units before placing the order with a known payment card and the home address (addresses are only read, never updated/deleted). The task asks no question, so complete_task takes no answer; its extra parameters are the ordered record objects only. supervisor-complete-task is forced last via (not (task-completed)) on every action.
